company_name: News Corporation (ASX CDI, Class B voting line; files USD 10-K as NWS/NWSA on Nasdaq)

inputs.share_count_basis: 541.05m basic at 31-Jul-2026 (10-K cover: 360,503,747 Class A + 180,548,891 Class B; 1 CDI = 1 share) plus 1.9m dilutive effect of equity awards (Note 14, FY2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. FY2026 buybacks ($641m) far exceed SBC ($77m) so the actual count is falling ~4%/yr; that is a modelling convention the company is more than funding, not un-funded dilution.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2026 Note 13 'Total equity compensation expense' $77m (FY2025 $84m, FY2024 $91m). No combined SBC-plus-withholding figure is published and net-share-settlement tax withholding is not a separate cash-flow line (it sits inside financing 'Other, net' $(53)m); sbc_incl_equity_taxes = 77 x ~1.10 = 85 is a documented estimate for that withholding. History: FY19 73, FY20 69, FY21 128 (cash-settled award mark-to-market), FY22 59, FY23 92 as-reported (87 restated ex-Foxtel in the FY2025 10-K), FY24 91, FY25 84, FY26 77.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are USD (10-K). The ASX quote is AUD. USD->AUD 1.4219 = 1/0.7033 AUDUSD=X (Yahoo, 2026-09-24T09:00Z). Parity check: Nasdaq NWS (Class B) US$ close 2026-09-23 x 1.4219 ties to the ASX NWS.AX close within 0.1%, confirming (i) NWS.AX references the Class B line, (ii) the rate direction, (iii) the quote basis. Per-share values are computed in USD then multiplied by fx_rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are AUD, the _usd twins are the model currency.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-denominated flows, so a USD WACC: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.05 (diversified media / information services; AUD and GBP earnings add translation variance) = cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% on the 2026 Facilities and 3.875%/5.125% notes, ~4.0% after tax; debt ~11% of capital -> 8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality (housing, book hits), AI-disintermediation and governance risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), as US GAAP already does it: operating lease cost ($109m FY2026, Note 10) is inside operating expenses/SG&A and therefore already deducted inside Segment EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($840m non-current + current portion) are EXCLUDED from total_debt. Finance leases are immaterial. Nothing is deducted twice: lease_cost_pct_path is left at 0 because the charge is already in the EBITDA margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: REA Group is 62.0% owned (10-K FY2026 p.3; up from 61.4% after REA's own $141m buyback). Consolidated flows include 100% of REA; the 38% minority (plus REA India / Planitar minorities) took $170m of $743m FY2026 continuing net income = 22.9%. Charged ONCE, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED rate 1 - (1 - cash tax)(1 - NCI leakage) = 1 - 0.73 x 0.77 = 43.8% in year 1, drifting to 45.3% (leakage 25%) by year 10 as REA compounds faster than the group. Calibration: FY2026 EBIT (Segment EBITDA 1,627 - SBC 85 - D&A 485 = 1,057) x (1 - 0.438) = $594m vs attributable net income $573m after $113m impairment/restructuring and $8m equity losses -- ties within non-operating noise. The $710m NCI book value is deliberately NOT deducted in the bridge, and REA's market value is NOT deducted either (see valuation_philosophy: deducting a ~45x-earnings market value for the minority against flows the DCF capitalises at 15x FCF would over-deduct).
inputs.interest_income_note: Segment EBITDA is pre-interest and net debt is bridged, so the FY0 owner-FCF base must be unlevered: NET interest income of $29m (interest income on the $2.1bn cash pile less ~$90m interest paid on borrowings) is stripped from reported FCF. Net cash is only $106m (well under 1x the FCF base) so the double-count would be small either way; the strip is for consistency with the EBITDA-based forward build.
inputs.working_capital_note: Working capital has CONSUMED cash every year since the Foxtel exit: FY2024 -$139m, FY2025 -$206m, FY2026 -$145m (receivables growth at Dow Jones licensing and REA outrunning the +$45m/yr deferred-revenue build). Modelled as a negative capture on the revenue change (-15% base) rather than the prepaid-subscription positive default.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route, engine-built) on CONTINUING-OPERATIONS consolidated flows, FY0 = FY2026 (30-Jun-2026). Routing: News Corp is an operating company whose value is a stream of segment cash flows (Dow Jones, REA/Move, HarperCollins, News Media); it is not a book-value holdco, so the BVPS-compounding row does not apply. The 'straddles two rows' clause is handled by (a) charging the listed REA minority once via leakage and (b) reporting the sum-of-the-parts with REA at market as a MEMO in valuation_philosophy, not as the house value. FOXTEL BREAK: Foxtel (Subscription Video Services) was sold to DAZN on 2-Apr-2025 and is discontinued from the FY2025 10-K onward; FY2024-FY2026 revenue (8,252 / 8,452 / 9,028) and Segment EBITDA (1,241 / 1,415 / 1,627) are continuing-ops and NOT comparable to the FY2015-FY2023 as-reported rows in Metrics.csv, which include Foxtel (FY2023 as-reported 9,879 vs 8,012 continuing per the FY2025 10-K segment note). FY2025 net income of $1,180m includes the $716m pre-tax ($692m after-tax) gain on the Foxtel sale in discontinued operations; FY2026 ($573m attributable, $743m consolidated) is the clean base. AI LICENSING: OpenAI (~$250m/5yr) and Meta (~$150m/3yr) are inside Dow Jones / News Media revenue and inside the $1,259m remaining performance obligations ($487m due FY2027); treated as a growth driver in the FY2027-FY2029 path and the bull case, not as a perpetual baseline -- the bear case assumes the 3-5 year terms are not renewed at scale. Quoted as A$ per CDI; model currency USD.
inputs.data_vintage: 10-K FY2026 (fiscal year ended 30-Jun-2026, filed Aug-2026) for all P&L, cash-flow, balance-sheet and share-count anchors; Q4 FY2026 call (5-Aug-2026) for qualitative guidance via Analysis.json; no FY2027 quantitative guidance has been issued.

equity_bridge.item: Investments (equity affiliates, ~6% DAZN stake received on the Foxtel sale, China and other equity securities) at 30-Jun-2026 carrying value
equity_bridge.note: 10-K FY2026 balance sheet, Note 6. Their income (equity losses -$8m, equity-security marks -$20m in Other, net) sits OUTSIDE Segment EBITDA, so by the matching-asset rule the assets enter the bridge. Carrying value (equity method / cost less impairment) is the conservative mark; a small share is held via REA and so partly belongs to the minority.
10-K FY2026 balance sheet, Note 17; unfunded pension/OPEB net liability deducted as debt-like.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr on the continuing-ops basis (FY2023 8,012 -> FY2026 9,028, both ex-Foxtel per the FY2025/FY2026 10-K segment notes), lifted to ~5% for the segment mix: Dow Jones +7%, Digital Real Estate +12%, Book Publishing +6%, News Media +3% in FY2026, with FX (AUD/GBP) a FY2027 tailwind. Equity CAGR is rejected as the anchor: equity has been flat for five years because $1.3bn of buybacks, dividends, the FY2020/FY2018 impairments and the Foxtel disposal offset retained earnings -- it describes capital return, not business growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.2-1.1%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (4.1% continuing) and from EPS; EPS CAGRs (58% 3yr, 13% 5yr) are meaningless because the FY2021 and FY2023 bases were depressed by impairment and restructuring charges. The 5-year revenue and FCF CAGRs are NEGATIVE only because FY2021 includes Foxtel (~$1.9bn revenue) and FY2026 does not; they are not evidence of shrinkage. Use the continuing-ops 3-year figures.

owner_fcf_series_usd_m.definition: reported FCF - SBC - net interest income (unlevered, matching the EBITDA-based forward build); FY2021-FY2023 include Foxtel, FY2024 onward are continuing ops

historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (5.5%) is below the reported-FCF 3yr CAGR (11.0%, 593 -> 811) mainly because FY2023 reported FCF carried $100m of net interest expense that has since reversed into $29m of net income -- balance-sheet deleveraging, not operating growth. SBC has FALLEN from $92m to $77m over the period, so SBC is not eating the growth here (the opposite of the DUOL pattern). Segment EBITDA grew 14.3%/yr on the continuing basis (1,089 -> 1,627), well ahead of revenue: margin expansion from 13.6% to 18.0% is the story of the last three years, and the base case assumes it continues at a slower pace, not that it repeats.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 6.0%: Dow Jones ~7-8% (Risk & Compliance +16-20%, $487m of RPO landing in FY2027 incl. AI licensing), Digital Real Estate ~9-10% (REA price/yield growth, Move premium products, AUD ~8% stronger than the FY2026 average), Book Publishing ~3%, News Media ~1%; tapers to 2.5% by year 9 as the AI-deal step-ups annualise and print keeps shrinking.
base.margin_rationale: 18.0% FY2026 -> 21.0% by FY2035. Dow Jones alone reaching management's $1bn EBITDA (FY2031) on ~$3.4bn revenue adds ~2pts to the group margin; REA mix adds ~1pt; News Media/print decline and Move investment take back ~1pt. Bull tests 24%, bear tests a stall at ~16.5%.
base.tax_rationale: Combined rate = cash tax 27% (FY2026 cash taxes $274m = 26% of pre-tax; GAAP ETR 29%; US 21% / AU 30% / UK 25% mix) x NCI leakage 23% -> 25% (REA grows faster than the group). See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2026 capex 4.7% / D&A 5.4% of revenue. D&A converges toward capex (acquired-intangible amortisation rolls off); capex eases to 4.5% post the Dow Jones platform and REA product spend.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 9%/2.5% = 15.8x FCF; capped at 15x, a multiple a buyer plausibly pays for a mixed portfolio of a 20x-plus data/marketplace franchise (Dow Jones, REA) and single-digit-multiple publishing and print. Terminal-year margin (21%) is flat for two years before capitalisation, so the 10-year horizon is long enough.

bull.narrative: Higher NCI leakage path (to 27%) because in this case REA is the fastest-growing piece; a 17x cap for a portfolio whose EBITDA is then ~60% Dow Jones + REA.

bear.narrative: Same WACC as base -- the risk is in the flows (growth stall, margin give-back, 12x cap for a business the market then reads as ex-growth media).

scenario_narratives.base: Dow Jones compounds toward management's $1bn Segment EBITDA (FY2026 $663m) on Risk & Compliance, Dow Jones Energy and near-record WSJ digital subscriptions; the OpenAI and Meta licences run their terms and are replaced by a mix of horizontal and vertical AI deals at broadly similar annual value rather than growing without limit. REA keeps 8-12% yield-led growth in a market it dominates; Move grows revenue high single digits on premium products while US existing-home sales stay subdued rather than recovering sharply. HarperCollins grows low-to-mid single digits on backlist and audio with hit-driven noise; News Media print decline continues at ~5%/yr, offset by digital so the segment is flat-to-slightly-down in dollars. Group margin climbs from 18.0% to 21% over a decade on mix. Working capital keeps absorbing ~15% of incremental revenue. The 38% REA minority takes 23-25% of after-tax flow throughout.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-licensing pipeline scales -- multiple additional LLM and vertical deals lift Dow Jones and News Media licensing revenue to a materially larger, largely costless stream -- while Risk & Compliance sustains high-teens growth and Dow Jones passes $1bn EBITDA ahead of FY2031. US housing normalises from multi-decade-low transaction volumes, lifting Move to a meaningful EBITDA contributor, and REA continues double-digit yield growth plus its own buybacks. Group margin reaches 24%; the capital-return programme keeps shrinking the count. The market re-rates the stub (Dow Jones, HarperCollins, News Media, Move) as an information-services business rather than a newspaper group -- the 17x cap reflects that, not a full sum-of-the-parts unlock, which would require a break-up the dual-class structure makes unlikely.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI answer-engines and summarisation erode referral traffic and subscription conversion at WSJ, The Times and the tabloids faster than licensing fees offset, and the 3-5 year OpenAI/Meta deals are renewed at lower value or not at all as the courts settle fair use in the platforms' favour. US existing-home sales stay depressed and Australian listing volumes soften, so Digital Real Estate growth slows to mid single digits; a weak publishing slate and continued print decline leave Book Publishing and News Media flat-to-down. Margin gives back to 16.5% as digital investment and journalist costs outrun revenue. Governance -- the Murdoch Family Trust's ~41% vote and the unresolved succession -- keeps any sum-of-the-parts discount from closing, so the terminal cap is 12x. Working capital absorbs 20% of the (small) revenue growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear lifted to 20% because two of the bear axes -- AI disintermediation of news traffic and the time-limited nature of the current AI licences -- are structural and outside management's control, and the dual-class structure removes the activist/break-up route that would otherwise backstop a discount. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (AI pipeline scaling, a US housing recovery, and Dow Jones reaching $1bn early). Base 50%: twelve consecutive quarters of profit growth and a net-cash balance sheet make the central path the most likely one; no going-concern, covenant or single-customer risk argues for more bear weight.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House value is a consolidated continuing-operations owner-FCF DCF, built from segment components (Segment EBITDA margin, SBC, D&A, capex, negative working-capital capture) with the REA Group minority charged once as a leakage on after-tax flows and the DAZN/other investment portfolio added in the bridge at carrying value. Three deliberate framing choices: (1) FOXTEL BREAK -- FY0 is FY2026, the first clean post-Foxtel year; FY2015-FY2023 as-reported rows include the pay-TV business and FY2025 net income carries the $692m after-tax disposal gain, so neither the long-run CAGRs nor FY2025 earnings are used as bases. (2) MINORITY INTEREST -- REA is 62% owned and consolidated; the minority's 38% is removed inside the flows (combined tax-plus-leakage rate 43.8% -> 45.3%), NOT by deducting the $710m NCI book value or REA's market value in the bridge, because charging both would double-count and deducting a market value that capitalises REA at ~45x earnings against flows the DCF capitalises at 15x FCF would over-deduct. (3) HOLDCO / SUM-OF-THE-PARTS -- reported as a MEMO, not the house value. At the 24-Sep-2026 REA.AX close (~A$20bn market cap, ~131.5m shares) the 62% stake is worth ~US$8.7bn; against a ~US$15.7bn blended enterprise value (Class A and Class B at their respective Nasdaq closes, plus the net-debt/investments bridge) that leaves the stub -- Dow Jones ($663m EBITDA), HarperCollins ($287m), News Media ($139m), Move (~breakeven) less corporate ($203m), ~$886m of EBITDA -- implied at roughly US$7bn or ~8x EBITDA. Management's 'materially undervalued on a sum-of-the-parts basis' claim is that Dow Jones alone deserves a mid-teens-plus multiple. The house DCF disagrees with the market mainly about REA: the model's consolidated flows give REA's 62% share a ~15x FCF exit, the market pays ~45x earnings for the listed line. A reader who believes REA's market multiple is durable should add roughly (REA market value of the stake minus its DCF-implied value) per share to the house figure; the spread between house IV and the price is largely that one judgment plus the holding-company discount the dual-class structure sustains.
key_risks_to_valuation: REA multiple: the largest single driver of the gap between house IV and the market price is whether REA's ~45x earnings multiple is a durable asset value or a premium the model should not capitalise; the leakage approach values the minority's share at the same 15x FCF as the rest of the consolidated flows.

AI licensing durability: OpenAI (~$250m/5yr) and Meta (~$150m/3yr) are inside the FY2027-FY2029 revenue path via RPO; the base assumes renewal at similar annual value, the bear assumes step-down. Roughly $80-130m/yr of near-costless EBITDA is at stake, ~1pt of group margin.
Working-capital sign: three consecutive years of cash absorption are modelled as continuing (-15% of revenue growth); if receivables normalise the base is ~$80m/yr too low.
Combined tax/leakage rate: a 2pt error in NCI leakage (e.g. REA outgrowing the group faster than assumed) moves attributable FCF ~3%.
Currency: model in USD, quote in AUD at 1.4219; a 5% AUD move shifts the A$ IV ~5% with no change in the business, and ~50% of revenue is AUD/GBP so the FX also flows through the USD flows.

Governance: Murdoch Family Trust ~41% voting control and the 2024 Starboard vote mean the sum-of-the-parts discount has no activist catalyst; a break-up or collapse of the dual-class structure is upside not in any scenario.

Buybacks at a price above house IV: $641m FY2026 repurchases are value-neutral in the model (flat count, SBC expensed) but in fact retire ~4%/yr of shares; if the market is right about REA they are accretive, if the house model is right they are executed above intrinsic value.

sotp_memo_inputs.note: Memo only; REA share count is approximate (post its FY2026 buyback). Not used in any scenario value.
